subject: ValenceRx — urgent regional failover request & exec standup
messages:
From: Ethan McGill <ethan@valencerx.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: ValenceRx Ops <ops@valencerx.com>, CISO ValenceRx <ciso@valencerx.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency + 5xx spike — US-WEST-2 (ValenceRx)

Connor / Monica —

We just started seeing a sharp jump in tail latency (p95 ~1.8s -> 8.5s) and elevated 5xx rate across our US-WEST-2 traffic at 09:08 PDT. Errors manifest as model inference timeouts and occasional kvcache misses that then cascade to retries from our side. This started right after your maintenance window in that AZ — not accusing, just correlating times.

We are seeing customer-facing failures (checkout API) and have paused a percentage of traffic, but our SLAs are being impacted. Can Redwood immediately divert our US-WEST-2 traffic to an alternate region or compatible model variant? We need a decision in 15 minutes.

I can provide traces and a sample of failing request ids (attached).

Urgent —
Ethan
Head of Platform
ValenceRx

Attachments: valencerx-p95-traces-20280729.log (log)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan McGill <ethan@valencerx.com>, ValenceRx Ops <ops@valencerx.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 09:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency + 5xx spike — US-WEST-2 (ValenceRx)

Ethan — thanks for the quick signal and the traces. We're looking at this now. Short update:

- Initial telemetry shows the spike is concentrated on a small set of GPU hosts in us-west-2 consumed by ValenceRx reserved pool. CPU and host-level IO look normal; inference kernel spikes imply a KV cache pressure pattern coupled with a queued-batching amplification.
- Monica is standing up a post-mortem bridge with our SREs.
- I want to avoid a blunt global failover unless we confirm model-compat/latency tradeoffs. Propose an ordered approach:
  1) Immediate regional steering: divert 40% of ValenceRx prod traffic from us-west-2 -> us-west-1 (model v2.1-quant) to reduce burst pressure.
  2) Activate prefix KV warming for warm sessions in the target region (to mitigate cold-kvcache misses).
  3) If error rate doesn't drop within 10 minutes of the steer, escalate to canary cross-region failover (60% -> us-west-1).

Monica — can your team authorize the initial 40% diversion? Marissa / Stephanie — looping you in for exec-level visibility; would like a short standup at 09:40 to confirm comms and credit/SLAs posture.

Connor
Product Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Ethan McGill <ethan@valencerx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency + 5xx spike — US-WEST-2 (ValenceRx)

Ethan / Connor —

Ethan, thanks for the traces — helpful. We've validated the pattern in our telemetry: a subset of model shards in us-west-2 experienced a short-lived KV cache thrash after a reclaim during the maintenance window which increased batch sizes for affected requests. That combination is producing the timeout surface you see.

We've approved the ordered approach Connor proposed. Immediate actions taken at 09:33 PDT:
- Diverting 40% of ValenceRx traffic from us-west-2 to us-west-1 (v2.1-quant).
- Triggered KV prefix warming on warm sessions in us-west-1; warming should reduce cold misses within ~3 minutes.
- Throttling auto-batch growth on the affected host set to cap batch size and prevent amplification.

Ethan — please confirm when you see error-rate and latency improvements on your side. We'll hold the canary plan as the next step if there is insufficient improvement by 09:50.

Also attaching a one-page geo-swap plan for exec review (proposed-geo-swap-plan.pdf). I'll be available on the standup at 09:40.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-geo-swap-plan.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan McGill <ethan@valencerx.com>, ValenceRx Ops <ops@valencerx.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ValenceRx — urgent regional failover request & exec standup

Team —

Thanks for the quick coordination. Brief exec note from my side for the standup summary (we kept it tight):

- Impact: ~18% of ValenceRx production requests saw >=1 retry; customer-visible p95 reduced from 8.5s -> 2.1s after 40% diversion and warming. No data-loss.
- Mitigation: regional diversion + kvcache warming + batching cap appear effective. We're holding further canary failovers in reserve.
- Customer asks: ValenceRx asked for an estimated time-to-normal (ETTN) and confirmation of whether any customer credits will be considered for the window.

Next actions (assigned):
- Monica: monitor the error curve for the next 2 hours and prepare a short RCA draft (targeted delivery 2028-07-30 10:00 PDT).
- Connor: coordinate with pricing/finance on credit exposure and run the impact calc for ValenceRx's committed capacity.
- Stephanie: prepare a two-sentence executive summary and the incident timeline for the account team to send to the ValenceRx CISO.

Ethan — we will follow up with the ETTN and proposed credit handling within 3 hours. Appreciate the fast signal and the samples you shared — helped us root cause much faster.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
